scope: Cross-layer materialization completion ordering: L1 byte/materialization support -> L3 scheduler/LoadedResource state publication
window_size_policy: Every 0x400 window is acquisition coverage only. It is not an asserted function-body size or semantic boundary.
non_claims: no generic fan-in counter or child-count mechanism is asserted
scheduler rollback is not relabeled as OS-level AsyncIO cancellation
state1/state2 are lifecycle states owned by L3 even when their ordering is supporting evidence for L1 materialization
successful byte-window acquisition alone does not prove original-process equivalence
the protected distribution executable is not substituted for the canonical analysis executable

windows.purpose: L1-support: reacquire caller-owned-destination whole-file transfer submission, submit failure and transport status writes.
L1-support: reacquire callback(ticketId,userContext,errorFlag,bytesRead), byte progress/status writes and any exact handoff into higher materialization/lifecycle scheduling.
L1/L3 boundary support: reacquire ReadRequest/FileSlot submission ownership and distinguish byte transport from request lifecycle.
L3 priority: reacquire scheduler pending-entry clear/rollback, queue matching and ordering; do not infer OS AsyncIO cancellation.
Cross-layer priority: close the resource materialization submission/scheduling wrapper body, callees and inherited load-context consumption without assuming a fan-in counter.
L3 priority: reacquire scheduler enqueue metadata, callback/context writes and ring ordering relative to materialization submission and completion callback registration.
L3 priority: reacquire scheduler callback execution and slot-clear ordering to identify the actual completion dependency mechanism.
L3 control path: reacquire exact cancellation sequence around scheduler rollback, state1/state2 to state4 writes and deferred cleanup enqueue.
Cross-layer seam: reacquire materialization dispatch success gate, state1 publication and completion callback registration ordering.
L1 priority when loose-list behavior is in scope: reacquire in-place child population, nested synthesis, child submission return handling and temporary/failure cleanup.
Explicit L1/L3 seam: reacquire representation/materialization mechanics and boolean return contract that gates L3 state1 publication.
L3 completion writer: reacquire callback context decoding, normal state1 to state2 publication and unusual tagged/sentinel branch without inventing semantics.
L3 control path: reacquire deferred state4 cleanup and backing-release ordering to complete the cancellation-side comparison.
